title: Google Adds an Independent Privacy Toggle for Gemini: Opt Out of AI Training While Retaining Chat History

content_html:
Google recently introduced a new privacy setting for the Gemini app, allowing users to independently control whether their chat content is used to train generative AI models while keeping their chat history. Previously, users who did not want their data used for training usually had to delete their chat history; now the two can be decoupled.

In practice, users can tap the settings icon in Gemini and find the newly added "Activity history" option at the bottom of the page. Tapping it takes them to the "Google My Activity" page, where they can turn the feature on or off via a drop-down menu.

Google says that after this feature is turned off, users' future chats will not be used to train generative AI models, except for "feedback content actively submitted by users." This means systematic collection of chat history can be blocked, but content users submit by actively clicking the "Feedback" button may still be included in training data.

This adjustment responds to users' long-standing concerns about transparency in how AI products use data. As regulatory frameworks such as the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act are gradually implemented, mainstream AI platforms are accelerating efforts to improve user data control mechanisms. By splitting "keeping records" and "participating in training" into two independent options, Google has lowered the barrier for users to manage their privacy and also provided the industry with a reference model for data governance.
